narrative:
The model estimates that you have a 37% chance of failing your final year. That is a risk flag, not a certainty: it means that among many students with a similar profile, about 37 in 100 would be expected not to pass. Because this risk is high enough to trigger the school’s support rule, you are being asked to take remedial courses.

The strongest reason behind the warning is your history of past class failures. You have one previous failure, while students who passed had an average of none. This was the most influential factor and it pushed the prediction toward failing. The second most important factor was your weekly study time. At five to ten hours, you are studying more than many students who passed, most of whom reported only two to five hours or less, so this factor pushed toward passing. The third factor was your intention to continue to higher education. You want to go on to higher education, as did all the passing students in this comparison, and this also pushed toward passing.

Even though study time and your ambition are helping, they were not enough to outweigh the past-failure signal. To improve your chances, take the remedial support seriously, keep a steady study routine, and ask your teachers or family for extra help early if a subject becomes difficult. Your goal of higher education is a real strength; use it to stay motivated.
